Platform that modernizes paper-based operations for new small-business owners

IB Index 7.0
·
B2B · SaaS
·

CONCEPT MOCKUP

BOOMER BUSINESSES IN…

2.3M-3M

US SMBs changing hands this decade

WHAT IT DEMANDS

THE PITCH

Someone just signed an SBA loan for $1.18M and bought a 30-year-old HVAC shop. Week one, the lead tech quits and takes two more techs. The office runs on paper tickets, a filing cabinet, and a bookkeeper who has been there since 1998. In FY2025 the SBA funded 7,003 of these acquisitions, up 35% year-over-year, and 59% of the buyers were first-timers. Nobody is selling them the handover.

WHO IT'S FOR

New owners in their first year after acquiring a traditional small business doing $500K+ ARR (ETA buyers, searchfunders, self-funded SMB acquirers taking over service, trades, or distribution shops).

THE GAP

Field service SaaS owns the software. Nobody owns the handover

WHY NOW

WHY NOW

SBA acquisition lending hit $8.29B in 2025, up 35% YoY, a program record

Two curves crossed in 2025. The number of first-time buyers taking over cash-flowing boomer businesses hit a record, and the cost of the software work needed to modernize those businesses collapsed. That is the window.

On the buyer side, FY2025 SBA 7(a) acquisition lending reached $8.29 billion across 7,003 deals, up 34.58% year-over-year, with the average acquisition loan at $1.18 million. The full 7(a) program hit $37.3 billion, a program record, and acquisition dollars were about 22% of the total, the largest share in at least three years. BizBuySell closed 9,586 listed transactions in 2025 with 59% of buyers first-time owners, and median days on market at 149, the fastest pace since 2017. The pipeline of boomer-to-younger-owner transfers is 2.3 to 3 million businesses over the next decade. The buyers are showing up now.

SOURCES
EBIT Community analysis of SBA data
CT Acquisitions analysis of SBA FYE25 data
BizBuySell 2025 Insight Report
Old National Bank
See the full timing case

MARKET SNAPSHOT

The receipts.

PAIN

7/10 SEVERITY

“People are messy. Deals are made up of people. So deals can be messy. When Carey Sobel asked me to pick one war story for this episode of M&A War Stories, honestly, it was hard to choose. Stories on the next episode (but not this one): → The bookkeeper who…”

X (JackieHirsch_) · JackieHirsch_

“Over the years, I've known a few small business owners who were old school and didn't trust computers and did everything by hand. All the inventory, every sale and every transaction…. all hand written and filed away. They're laughing their as*es off right…”

X (complicatedpast) · complicatedpast

“When me and my biz partner owned convenience stores in 4 states, we literally ran the whole thing on green sheets and a full time bookkeeper He was old school ha! Green sheets is how every business was ran until tech replaced it”

X (ChrisTwiggsPM) · ChrisTwiggsPM

All 8 receipts, and where these people gather

WHITESPACE

MARKET GAP

Field service SaaS owns the software. Nobody owns the handover

Understand the opening

THE WEDGE

Timing and service, not software: catch the buyer in the first 90 days when motivation is highest, and do the migration for them instead of selling another vertical SaaS seat alongside ServiceTitan, Jobber, Housecall Pro, etc.

The incumbent to beat: DueDilio

PROOF & SIGNALS

Stanford GSB's 2026 Search Fund Study tracks 862 US and Canadian core search funds since 1984 and identifies 181 new launches in 2024-2025 alone. Median 2024-25 acquisition: $16M enterprise value, $2.5M EBITDA, 25% margin, 30-40 employees.

STANFORD GSB 2026 SEARCH FUND STUDY

Old National Bank (citing broader industry data) estimates 2.3 to 3 million Baby Boomer-owned SMBs in the US will transition ownership over the next decade. These businesses employ about 32 million people and generate near $6.5 trillion in annual revenue; only about half of retiring owners have a formal succession plan.

OLD NATIONAL BANK

Accredited's 2026 analysis: BizBuySell has recorded a 20% decrease in boomer presence in the business-for-sale market since 2020, and Gen X and millennials now make up over 75% of business owners and over 80% of buyers entering small business ownership. Multiples have not fallen; competition for deals is up.

ACCREDITED (JOINACCREDITED.COM)

Calder Capital analysis of Stanford 2026 data: search fund acquisition rates fell from 86% for 2007-2010 vintages to about 48% for 2021-2024 vintages. More buyers compete for the same pool, median purchase price hit $16M in 2024-25 (near all-time high), and only speed wins: searchers who signed an LOI within six months closed at 74% vs 48% baseline.

CALDER CAPITAL (SUMMARIZING STANFORD GSB 2026)
Explore the evidence

WHO YOU'RE UP AGAINST

8 PLAYERS

ServiceTitan

: field service SaaS incumbent.

Jobber

: field service SaaS for solo and small crews.

Housecall Pro

: field service SaaS for home-service shops.

DueDilio

INCUMBENT

: marketplace of vetted post-acquisition specialists (accounting, technology/systems, operations, HR, legal) sold directly to new SMB owners.

Redpath and Company

: CPA firm with a dedicated ETA / Search Fund Advisory practice offering First 100 Days post-close execution (operational and organizational design, financial planning, change management, accounting/bookkeeping support).

Fetch Strategies

ETA Hub: 90-day cohort program for ETA buyers covering search, acquisition, and transition.

Seay HR

: fractional HR firm built specifically for ETA searchers.

SmallBizController

: fractional controller firm with an "Acquisition & Integration Support" line that promises to align systems, workflows, and reporting post-acquisition.

PEOPLE ARE ASKING FOR IT

REDDIT

“The lead technician, Ray, quit in the first week. He'd thought the owner was going to hand him the business. When he found out otherwise, he left. No QoE report could have told me the business was really Ray, and that the customers were loyal to Ray. Two more…”

X (MatznerJon) · MatznerJon

“They are looking at the industries that still have visible inefficiencies: service businesses, local retail, asset-heavy operations, parking, laundromats, and similar businesses. They will bring testing discipline, systems thinking, and optimization tools…”

X (lakshyabehl) · lakshyabehl

“Look at it through a first six months lens vs 100 days. (100 days is an arbitrary number anyway, likely stolen from US Presidents during their inaugural address.) Take the time to learn about your new business from the inside. Find out what you really have to…”

The Business Inquirer (Searchfunder repost) · The Business Inquirer / Searchfunder

THE VERDICT

Should you build this?

REASONS TO BUILD

The buyer cohort is at a record and funded: 7,003 SBA 7(a) acquisition loans in FY2025 at $8.29B, up 35% YoY, with 59% of BizBuySell buyers first-timers who need help.
Nobody is selling the 90-day done-for-you handover: ServiceTitan takes 3-12 months to onboard, Jobber and Housecall Pro are self-serve, and DueDilio is a marketplace not a product.
Service-firm pricing is already proven in this cohort: Fetch Strategies charges $4,000 for a 90-day cohort, Seay HR and SmallBizController both sell acquisition-integration retainers, so $7,500 setup plus $500/mo is in range.
The distribution is unglamorous but concrete: 20 SBA lender relationships, 10 broker agreements, and 5 ETA creators reach the whole first-year acquirer cohort without touching paid search.

REASONS TO NOT BUILD

Nobody searches for this: problem-language queries (just bought a business what now, modernize small business operations) return 0-20 US searches a month on Google Ads, so every customer is cold outreach.
The Search Fund 100-day plan tells new owners to wait six months before changing systems, which means the 90-day pitch fights the acquirer's own best-practice advice and attach on Operator Monthly could churn fast.
Jobber and Housecall Pro could kill this with a channel program: they have 275K combined monthly brand searches and could launch an acquirer partner network for less than $10M.
Service margins cap the business at a $12M-$15M lifestyle outcome; a founder who wants a venture-scale company will quit before year three.
Roast it with your agent

FOUNDER FIT

Not every good idea is good for you.

WHO IT’S BEST FOR

Solo operators with small-business software implementation or consulting expe...
Teams combining SaaS product skills with service-business operations expertise
Pure product founders without access to acquired small-business owners
Founders seeking a low-touch SaaS model before validating implementation costs

The founder who wins has already done this once. Either they ran a search, closed on a boomer business, and did their own 90-day migration, or they spent five-plus years in operations at a trades or distribution shop. They know a dozen SBA loan officers by first name, they have been on an M&A Twitter thread, and they are comfortable sitting at a kitchen table with a 58-year-old lead tech and getting him to write down what he knows. A SaaS-first founder loses here. The product is the person for the first 50 customers.

The value ladder.

Setup fee ($7,500) is anchored to DueDilio/Redpath/Seay HR service pricing, not to SaaS seat pricing. Monthly ($500) is below a fractional controller ($2K-$5K) and above a software seat ($39-$599), the uncontested middle. Free audit doubles as diligence help, which is where the acquirer actually wants a second opinion.

1

LEAD MAGNET

Week-One Takeover Audit(Free)

45-minute call plus one-page written audit of current systems, key-person risk, and the first 30-day break list. Works at closing week or during diligence.

2

FRONTEND

90-Day Takeover($7,500 one-time)

Done-for-you migration from paper and phone to scheduling, invoicing, CRM, and reviews on Jobber or Housecall Pro, plus QuickBooks cleanup. Tribal-knowledge interviews with the lead tech in week two.

3

CORE

Operator Monthly($500/mo)

Keep the stack running: new-hire training, monthly reporting, SaaS vendor management, quarterly review. The reason you still have the customer in month 13.

4

CONTINUITY

Vertical SaaS Migration($5,000 project)

View the full value ladder

THE PLAN

If you started today.
First up.

Nobody searches for a post-acquisition modernization bundle. The problem-language queries this idea needs (just bought a business what now, modernize small business operations, replace paper invoices small business) all return 0 to 20 US searches a month. The acquirer searches BizBuySell (165,000 a month), Jobber (201,000), Housecall Pro (74,000), and ServiceTitan (60,500), and self-serves from there. Content and SEO will not find them. The first 100 customers come one at a time, from the three places the acquirer is in the week they close.

If you started today.

Nobody searches for a post-acquisition modernization bundle. The problem-language queries this idea needs (just bought a business what now, modernize small business operations, replace paper invoices small business) all return 0 to 20 US searches a month. The acquirer searches BizBuySell (165,000 a month), Jobber (201,000), Housecall Pro (74,000), and ServiceTitan (60,500), and self-serves from there. Content and SEO will not find them. The first 100 customers come one at a time, from the three places the acquirer is in the week they close.
